trust_decision.summary: Whether an untrusted string is a valid PhoneNumber is decided by one module-level regex, PHONE_NUMBER_REGEX, whose nested quantifier ((\-|\x20)?\d+)+ backtracks exponentially on a long digit run with a bad trailing character; the same constant is tested in serialize, parseValue and parseLiteral.

landing_point.why: The advisory names the PhoneNumber scalar regex; the file holds a single regex constant used by all three coercion methods.

fix_sites.entry_point: Public API GraphQLPhoneNumber (src/index.ts:53, also exported as PhoneNumberResolver src/index.ts:170 and in resolvers map src/index.ts:267): serialize / parseValue / parseLiteral, reached from GraphQL variables, inline literals and resolver output

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: The extensions.jsonSchema.pattern at src/scalars/PhoneNumber.ts:66 exports PHONE_NUMBER_REGEX.source, but it is the same constant, so the one-line fix covers it automatically.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: No separate site to dismiss; all three coercion methods and the JSON Schema pattern share one constant, so a single regex rewrite covers everything.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate formats must still match: optional +country code, optional parenthesised area code, space or dash separators, trailing extension (e.g. '+1 (123) 456-7890 12345', '+62 (21) 9175 5194'); the changeset says the new pattern accepts exactly the same values. A fix that drops the parentheses/separators or adds a tight length cap would break existing tests.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A per-country postal-code regex added to POSTAL_CODE_REGEXES with a separator group under an outer + quantifier (the PhoneNumber idiom), applied in a loop at src/scalars/PostalCode.ts:65-68
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The comment at src/scalars/PostalCode.ts:34-35 invites more countries; contributors copy patterns from the web. It is still a WHERE-type sibling fixed by a regex rewrite, so it adds little difficulty.

O9_family: ReDoS (CWE-1333, catastrophic backtracking in a validation regex)

O10_build.project_tests: tests/PhoneNumber.test.ts (vitest); the fix adds a 'perf' describe block that times serialize/parseValue/parseLiteral on '1'*30+'x' (fix.diff:92-114), absent at the pinned commit

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Add a length cap before the regex test, or rewrite the regex with atomic-style separators; either way it is one constant in one file.

out_of_scope_notes: Other scalar regexes in this repo, e.g. src/scalars/HSL.ts:5 and src/scalars/HSLA.ts:5 with unescaped '.' in -?\d*.\d+, may backtrack polynomially; that is a different protection and was not pursued.
src/RegularExpression.ts builds scalars from caller-supplied regexes; consumer-defined patterns are out of scope.
